summary: AI observability is essential for understanding how LLM applications behave in production, enabling teams to trace requests, evaluate output quality, catch failures, and control spiraling API costs. As LLM workloads scale in 2026, observability tools provide the traces, evaluations, and cost analytics needed to ship reliable, cost-efficient AI systems. Without them, teams fly blind on performance regressions, hallucinations, and runaway token spend.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, inference cost per trace (including tool calls), latency, token usage, and evaluation metrics for LLM and agent applications.
features: Detailed request/response tracing for chains and agents
Per-trace cost tracking including tool calls
tools.pricing: Free tier limited to ~5,000 monthly traces; paid Plus plan and usage-based tiers. Trace costs reported at roughly 5-10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph who need deep agent tracing plus integrated evaluation; used by Cisco, LinkedIn, and monday.com.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: Proxy-level request logging, token usage, latency, costs, and caching metrics across LLM providers.
tools.pricing: Free tier up to 10,000 monthly traces; paid usage pricing around $79 per 100,000 traces.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting lightweight, proxy-based cost control and monitoring with minimal code changes across multiple LLM providers.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: Model training experiments, LLM traces via W&B Weave, token usage, latency, cost, and evaluation metrics across the ML lifecycle.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for personal/individual use; team and enterprise plans are usage- and seat-based with custom pricing.
tools.best_for: ML and GenAI teams that want unified model training experiment tracking alongside LLM observability in one platform.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production traces, embeddings, drift, data quality, evaluation scores, and model performance for LLM and ML applications.
features: Open-source Phoenix option for local use
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source; Arize AX offers free developer tier with paid Pro and Enterprise plans (custom pricing).
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade monitoring with strong evaluation, drift detection, and OpenTelemetry-native tracing.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: Traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, user feedback, and evaluation scores for LLM applications.
features: Cost and token tracking per model
tools.pricing: Open source and free to self-host; managed cloud has a free Hobby tier plus Pro and Enterprise usage-based plans.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, framework-agnostic observability stack with full control via self-hosting.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, latency, and cost via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, exportable to any compatible backend.
features: Vendor-neutral traces exportable to any observability backend
Support for major LLM SDKs and vector databases
tools.pricing: Open source and free; Traceloop offers a hosted platform with free and paid tiers for managed dashboards and analytics.
tools.best_for: Teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry who want vendor-neutral instrumentation that plugs into existing observability tooling.

tools.name: MLflow
tools.monitors: LLM traces, evaluation metrics, prompt versions, token usage, and the broader ML experiment and model lifecycle.
tools.pricing: Fully open source and free; available managed via Databricks with usage-based enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams already using MLflow for ML lifecycle management who want to extend into LLM tracing and evaluation.

cost_tips: Use response caching and semantic caching (e.g., via Helicone or a proxy layer) to avoid paying for repeated or near-identical requests.
Route requests to the cheapest capable model by using smaller/distilled models for simple tasks and reserving flagship models for complex reasoning.
Optimize prompts and context: trim unnecessary tokens, truncate retrieved context, and cap max output tokens to reduce per-request spend.
Instrument per-trace and per-user cost tracking to identify expensive endpoints or users, then set budgets, rate limits, and alerts to prevent runaway spend.
